source_text: Nam si, ut et superior sermo patefecit, et secuturus docebit, quidquid ratio est, quidquid eruditio, quidquid iustitia, quidquid pietas, quidquid testimoniorum sacrorum, huic quod tuemur dogmati suffragatur; nihil aliud inimici nostri toto adipiscuntur conatu, quam ut doctis quibusque impudentissimi, sanctis contumacissimi, in Deum profanissimi comprobentur.
pass_a_gloss: For if, as both the earlier speech has opened and the one about to follow will teach, whatever is reason, whatever learning, whatever justice, whatever piety, whatever of sacred testimonies, votes for this dogma which we guard; our enemies by their whole effort obtain nothing else than that they be proved most shameless to all the learned, most stubborn to the holy, most profane toward God.
pass_b_english: For if, as the preceding discussion has shown and the following discussion will show, everything belonging to reason, learning, justice, devotion, and the testimony of sacred Scripture supports the doctrine we defend, all our enemies’ efforts achieve nothing except to prove them utterly shameless before every learned person, utterly defiant before the holy, and utterly irreverent toward God.

choices.why: Julian's forensic virtue that renders to each his own, without fraude or gratia (partiality).
rejected: righteousness (Pauline overlay unless the verse forces it)

choices.why: Proof-text, especially Rom 5:12 in this book; keep 'testimony' not 'verse'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
